evidence: http.py:285-292: marked_send copies the message, uses message.get('headers', []) so a missing key is tolerated, filters any existing x-sqllens-auth via k.lower() != b'x-sqllens-auth' (so the appended header is duplicate-free), and sets a new list of (bytes, bytes) tuples. The ASGI spec defines headers as an iterable of [bytes, bytes] and servers accept lists of tuples; Starlette responses emit raw_headers as a list of byte tuples with lowercase names. The assumptions hold. I did not run the code against uvicorn or FastMCP; this rests on the ASGI spec and Starlette's known behavior.

http.py:285 declares marked_send(message: dict) and passes it at :294 as Send. Starlette's Send is Callable[[Message], Awaitable[None]] with Message = MutableMapping[str, Any] (from my knowledge; starlette/types.py not in the view and not read). A param typed dict is narrower than MutableMapping, so a strict type checker would reject it by contravariance. Runtime is fine since ASGI servers send plain dicts, and the code does dict(message). No requirement (repo type-check rule) was shown, and no mypy/pyright run was done.

http.py:246-250: normalized=_PathNormalizer(_AuthMiddleware(inner)); marked=_InsecureAuthMarker(normalized) when insecure_bind; returned TrustedHostMiddleware(marked,...). So marker is inside the host guard and outside _PathNormalizer, hence wraps its /healthz, /readyz short-circuits and the / 307 redirect (marked_send decorates every http.response.start, lines 285-292). TrustedHostMiddleware rejects bad Host with its own 400 before calling the inner app, so no marker there. The marker exists only in insecure-opt-out mode (the claim's context); the docstring at 222-224 matches.

policy.py:27-35. For str inputs: only 'localhost' (case-insensitive) or a parsed loopback IP returns True; wildcards ('0.0.0.0','::',''), other hostnames, and malformed strings raise ValueError from ip_address and return False. None/int raise AttributeError on .lower(), caught -> False. IPv4-mapped IPv6 is explicitly unwrapped at lines 33-34 via ipv4_mapped.is_loopback, independent of Python version behavior. Input-trace: a hostile object whose .lower() raises RuntimeError would propagate, and 4-byte bytes would be parsed as packed IPv4 (so 127.0.0.1 bytes returns True), but neither is producible by a shipped caller (the only caller, unauthenticated_non_loopback, line 40, passes cfg.server.host, a configured string), so they do not count against the claim.

http.py:250 wraps _InsecureAuthMarker (only when insecure_bind) inside TrustedHostMiddleware and outside _PathNormalizer/_AuthMiddleware/FastMCP, so every Host-accepted http scope, including /healthz, /readyz and /mcp responses, goes through marked_send (lines 285-294), which sets x-sqllens-auth: insecure-loopback-override on every http.response.start (replacing any existing). FastMCP responses are covered by the marker, not _send_json. Reminder: logged when _last_warning is None (first request) or >=60s elapsed (278-283). The read-check-write has no await, so asyncio concurrency cannot interleave it; no lock is needed. _send_json (724-743) adds x-content-type-options: nosniff to health, readiness and 401 responses. Input traced: concurrent requests crossing the 60s boundary. Only one task runs between read and write, so one warning is logged.

http.py:249-250 wraps marker inside TrustedHostMiddleware (so only Host-accepted requests reach it). _InsecureAuthMarker (266-294): non-http scopes pass through (274-276); logs when _last_warning is None or >=60s elapsed (277-283); stamps x-sqllens-auth: insecure-loopback-override on http.response.start (285-291). _send_json (724-743) adds nosniff; it is the sole writer used by health/readiness (status) and _send_401 (auth errors) (749,762,772). Lifespan/websocket scopes reaching the marker are passed through. Doc claim matches code.

auth/policy.py:21-35 is_loopback_host: 'localhost' (case-insensitive) returns True before any DNS; otherwise ipaddress.ip_address parses (no DNS), IPv4-mapped IPv6 is unwrapped and checked via ipv4_mapped.is_loopback, else address.is_loopback (covers 127.0.0.0/8 and ::1). Invalid/other hostnames fail closed. transport/http.py:240-242 in _build_asgi_app_bare: insecure_bind = unauthenticated_non_loopback(cfg) (auth.mode none and non-loopback, policy.py:38-40, independent of transport); raises ValueError if insecure_bind and not cfg.auth.insecure. build_asgi_app (line 183) calls _build_asgi_app_bare unconditionally and run (line 257) calls build_asgi_app, none of them checking server.transport, so stdio config is still guarded. Counter-input tried: host '::ffff:127.0.0.1' and '127.5.5.5' both loopback; '0.0.0.0' rejected unless insecure.

http.py:246-250: normalized=_PathNormalizer(_AuthMiddleware(inner, authenticator)); marked=_InsecureAuthMarker(normalized) only if insecure_bind else normalized; returned TrustedHostMiddleware(marked, ...).
